sections.content: How many people stayed in Liverpool after gaining qualifications?

Liverpool is a city in the North West. Liverpool also has a university.

Liverpool has higher levels of deprivation.

Overall, Liverpool ended up with:

  • more graduates than it produced
  • a similar number of non-graduates with advanced qualifications as it produced
Note: all towns and cities in this analysis are defined based on population size only. This means that some cities are classed as towns because of their population.

Let's explore this further

There were 25,415 state-school pupils from Liverpool who sat their GCSEs between the 2007 to 2008 and the 2010 to 2011 school years.

Of these, 7,575 (30%) went on to gain degree-level qualifications (level 6+ as defined by The Office of Qualifications and Examinations Regulation, or Ofqual ). We will call these people graduates.

Another 7,195 (28%) went on to gain other advanced post-16 qualifications, such as A-Levels, a foundation degree or higher apprenticeship (levels 3-5 as defined by Ofqual). In this tool, we will refer to these non-graduates with advanced qualifications as “qualified non-graduates", for brevity.

The charts below compare Liverpool to other English towns and cities using three measures:

  • what proportion of Liverpool's pupils became graduates or qualified non-graduates by the 2017 to 2018 academic year
  • of those graduates and qualified non-graduates, the percentages that lived in Liverpool in the 2018 to 2019 academic year
  • how many graduates and qualified non-graduates from elsewhere came to live there by 2018 to 2019, relative to the number who sat their GCSEs there

In some towns, some of this information may not be available because of small sample sizes.
The size and deprivation level of a town, as well as the qualification levels of older residents, were all related to students' educational attainment. Read our previous analysis.

Where did those who left Liverpool move to?

Of Liverpool's graduates, 1,315 were living elsewhere in 2018/19.

However, 185 of those graduates (14%) were living fairly locally, in the Liverpool travel to work area (TTWA).

Of Liverpool's qualified (level 3+) non-graduates, 790 were living elsewhere in 2018/19.

However, 295 of those qualified non-graduates (37%) were living fairly locally, in the Liverpool travel to work area (TTWA).

Of those in Liverpool's GCSE cohort:

  • 835 graduates left the North West
  • the most common region they moved to was London
  • 285 qualified (level 3+) non-graduates left the North West
  • the most common region they moved to was London

In 2018 to 2019, 34% of graduates and 15% of qualified non-graduates living in Liverpool had moved there from elsewhere

In the 2018 to 2019 academic year, there were 9,250 graduates and 7,375 qualified (level 3+) non-graduates from our cohort living in Liverpool. This is compared with the 7,575 graduates and 7,195 qualified non-graduates who had lived there when they sat their GCSEs.

In 2018 to 2019, 66% of the graduates had also lived in Liverpool as GCSE pupils, while 34% had moved there from elsewhere.

Of the qualified non-graduates who lived in Liverpool in 2018 to 2019, 85% had lived there as GCSE pupils, while 15% had moved to the area from elsewhere.
